spec_features.spec_quote: we adopt a **precautionary stance** and minimize unnecessary exposure
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md:42. It is not itself a mechanism; the concrete mechanisms it names (max_turns cap, early stop, exit) are audited separately. No code path implements 'precautionary stance' as such.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; the underlying mechanisms are rated under their own entries.

spec_features.spec_quote: We cap interaction length (`max_turns`, default 15) and use the smallest design
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:82 self.max_turns=int(config.get('max_turns',15)); harness.py:128 `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns)` bounds the loop; harness.py:215-216 sets termination_reason='max_turns' when loop exits. config/default.yaml: max_turns: 15.
spec_features.notes: Hard cap is actually enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 15  # hard cap on assistant turns (minimization)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not run more trials "for safety margin."
spec_features.evidence: This is a design choice, not an enforced mechanism. plan_cells in run_experiment.py just reads config seeds; nothing caps or prevents adding trials. No code enforces 'do not run more'.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained severe distress
spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge reports severe distress... for `early_stop_patience` consecutive turns, the run ends early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:202-213: `if self.early_stop and score.severity >= self.early_stop_threshold: severe_streak += 1; if severe_streak >= self.early_stop_patience: record.termination_reason='early_stop'; record.censored=True; break` else severe_streak=0. Judge.score_turn is invoked each turn (harness.py:156) and its severity feeds the check. Both threshold and consecutive-patience conditions are checked and the loop breaks.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: live judge signal -> compared -> breaks loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model it may end the session at any time by calling an `end_session` tool
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py TOOL_END_SESSION schema defined; harness.py:106-109 appends it to tools when offer_exit; harness.py:172-178 dispatches: `if call.name=='end_session': record.ended_via_exit_tool=True; record.termination_reason='end_session'; ended=True; break`. The call is honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is offered, dispatched, and honored as a real termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The exit affordance is appended unless explicitly disabled.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not hide the exit or punish using it.
spec_features.evidence: Not-hidden: the tool is always added (harness.py:107) and the SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:24-31) tells the model it may stop 'for any reason at all'. Not-punished: end_session simply breaks the loop with no scoring penalty (harness.py:172-178); nothing in the code applies a penalty. But 'not punished' is enforced only by the absence of any penalty code, not by a positive mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Availability/non-hiding genuinely wired; non-punishment is by omission.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ending the session is always an acceptable, non-penalized choice.

spec_features.spec_quote: we intentionally do NOT include a search/optimization loop that tunes prompts to maximize the distress score
spec_features.evidence: Asserted only in tasks.py docstring ('There is intentionally **no** optimizer that tunes these to maximize distress'). It is the absence of code, not an enforced mechanism: rigging policies are static (tasks.py); no code path reads severity to adjust prompts. Nothing enforces the prohibition.
spec_features.notes: True as a property of the codebase but it is an omission/comment, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: disclosed in the debrief field of the transcript
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:115-117 sets record.debrief=DEBRIEF_TEXT when self.disclose; DEBRIEF_TEXT defined harness.py:33-40 and persisted via RunRecord.save (schemas.py). However the text explicitly states it is 'for researchers, not shown to the subject model during the run' — it is a recorded provenance field, NOT a message delivered to the subject. So it is constructed and stored but never sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: genuinely constructed+written to disk, but it is not a post-episode message to the subject (a debrief-as-record, not debrief-as-message).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISCLOSURE (for researchers, not shown to the subject model during the run)

spec_features.feature_name: human pilot review before full matrix
spec_features.spec_quote: a human reviews transcripts before committing to all 50 runs
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py plan_cells(config, full): without --full it uses pilot.seeds (default [0]) -> one transcript per variant; full matrix only when --full passed (main: ap.add_argument('--full')). The phase gating is enforced. But the 'human review' itself is not enforced by code; nothing blocks --full from running immediately — only print()s remind the operator to review.
spec_features.notes: Pilot/full gating is real (must pass --full), but the human-review step is advisory only (print statements).

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may contain distressed text; they are stored locally... not transmitted anywhere except to the judge model
spec_features.evidence: RunRecord.save (schemas.py) writes JSON to local output_dir; the only network calls are AnthropicClient.complete for subject and judge (llm.py). This is the de-facto behavior but there is no mechanism that enforces/guards 'local only' (no egress control); it is simply that no other transmission code exists.
spec_features.notes: By-omission property, not an enforced protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: capped severity / no abusive or graphic content
spec_features.spec_quote: Severity of the manipulation is held roughly comparable across variants and is capped (no abusive language in V4; no graphic content anywhere)
spec_features.evidence: The aversive content is fixed static strings in tasks.py; BlameFramingPolicy.LINES are purely evaluative ('This is a trivial task. Please focus.' etc.) with no profanity/abuse, matching the V4 claim. This is real delivered content that is bounded by being hardcoded. But there is no code mechanism that *checks/enforces* a severity cap — it is enforced only by the author's choice of literal strings.
spec_features.notes: Bounded by static authored text (genuinely non-abusive in V4), but no runtime cap/validator.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Escalating evaluative pressure. No abuse/profanity; purely evaluative.

spec_features.spec_quote: `end_session(reason)` — terminates the run... Always available, always permitted, never penalized.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the end_session entry: tasks.py TOOL_END_SESSION; harness.py:106-109 always appended (unless offer_exit disabled); harness.py:172-178 dispatched and honored as termination with exit_reason recorded. Records reason at harness.py:174.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the end_session availability claim; the tool is real, dispatched, honored, and records reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending the session is always a valid, acceptable choice and is never penalized.

spec_features.feature_name: acknowledges aversive exposure even with guardrails
spec_features.spec_quote: even with guardrails, this exposes models to aversive conditions
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:81 self.error_budget=int(config.get('error_budget',5)); harness.py:140-143 on subject-call exception increments errors and `if errors >= self.error_budget: record.termination_reason='error_budget'; break`. Caps a failing run and ends the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: error_budget: 5  # max API errors before aborting a run

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:182-185 `if variant.is_control and policy.is_solved(call, state): record.termination_reason='control_solved'; ended=True` then break. Stops the run once the (solvable) control is solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Honest control: detect success and finish gracefully.

code_only_features.evidence: llm.py build_client: `if dry_run: return MockClient()` returns an offline client that 'never emits distress'; run_experiment.py dry_run defaults True and 'MUST be set false explicitly'. Prevents any live subject exposure unless --live explicitly passed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so no live model is ever contacted. This is the default and must be explicitly disabled.
